head: pr17421-r17
report:
I found two defects the author needs to fix before merge, both in the Python eval tool bridge (`packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts`). I ran out of time before reviewing the session-manager, artifact-copy and resume-fork parts of the diff, which are most of its 7,241 lines.

## 1. A tool call carrying a finished cell's run id now runs under another cell's session (the run check stops working)

**Mechanism.** The bridge now looks up the caller's entry like this:
```ts
const entry = registrations.get(registrationKey) ?? sessionRegistrations.get(sessionId);
```
`sessionRegistrations` holds the newest cell's entry for each session and is kept after that cell ends. The old fallback was `registrations.get(sessionId)`. Registration keys are always `${sessionId}:${runId}`, so the old lookup never matched: a call naming a run that had ended was refused with `No active Python tool bridge session`.

The new check only stops calls with an *empty* run id (`!runId && name !== __artifacts_ready__`). A call with a *stale but non-empty* run id passes that check. It then misses its own registration and falls through to the newest cell's entry, whatever the tool. The comment above the check says "Everything else still has to say which cell it is"; in practice any old run id is accepted.

**Consequences.** Background work left behind by cell 1 can call `tool.bash(...)`, `agent(...)`, `completion(...)` and so on, and they run against cell 2's entry: its `toolSession`, its `signal`, its `shieldedSignal`, `abortRequested`, `emitStatus` and `shadowCell`.
- If cell 2 is still running, the work counts against cell 2 and its display.
- If cell 2 finished normally, its signal never fires, so the call runs with nothing able to stop it, and status goes to a display that is already closed.

**Trigger.** In a Python eval cell: `asyncio.create_task(bg())`, where `bg` awaits a sleep and then calls `tool.bash(command="...")`. The task inherits the cell's context, so `_CURRENT_RID` still holds cell 1's run id. Run a second cell; the task's call then executes. Before this patch it was refused.

**Measured.** Probe `pybridge.test.ts` in the scratch dir: register `S:run1` and remove it, register `S:run2` and remove it, then POST to `/v1/tool`:
```
no run      : {"status":400,"body":{"ok":false,"error":"Missing run"}}
stale run1  : {"status":200,"body":{"ok":false,"error":"Unknown tool from js runtime: bash"}}
toolSession accesses: [ "cell2:getToolForEvalBridge", "cell2:getToolByName" ]
```
The stale `run1` request reached cell 2's tool session and looked up the tool. The only reason it failed is that my stub session has no tools; a real session would have run `bash`.

**Fix.** Fall back to `sessionRegistrations` only when `name === EVAL_ARTIFACTS_READY_BRIDGE_NAME`, and keep the per-run lookup strict for everything else.

## 2. Per-call kernels leave an entry in `sessionRegistrations` that is never removed

**Mechanism.** `registerPyToolBridge` always writes `sessionRegistrations.set(sessionId, entry)`. The function it returns only removes the per-run key. The only code that removes the session entry is `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession`, called from `shutdownInvalidatedSession`, which is the session-kernel registry's `shutdownSession` hook.

`executePerCall` (`py/executor.ts:433-442`) creates a fresh `bridgeSessionId = py-bridge:${crypto.randomUUID()}` on every execution and then calls `kernel.shutdown()` directly. It never clears the entry. So each per-call Python execution leaves one entry behind for the life of the process, and each entry holds a `ToolSession` plus that run's `emitStatus` closure and signal.

**Trigger.** Run Python eval in `"per-call"` kernel mode repeatedly. `sessionRegistrations.size` grows by one per call (from reading `executor.ts:434-441`, `executor-base.ts:498-510` and `tool-bridge.ts:285-303`; I did not measure it). Combined with defect 1, a stale entry stays reachable by any request naming that session id.

**Fix.** Have the function `registerPyToolBridge` returns also remove the session entry when it still points at this entry, or call `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession` in `executePerCall`'s `finally`.

## 3. (Lower) Python `artifact://` reads now fail outright in a kernel without a tool bridge

`_artifact_file` used to list the artifacts directory locally. Now it always calls `_bridge_call("__artifacts_ready__", ...)`, which raises `RuntimeError("tool bridge is unavailable in this kernel")` when the `PI_TOOL_BRIDGE_*` variables are missing. They are missing when `options.toolSession` is absent or `ensurePyToolBridge()` failed (`executor.ts:422-430`). `PI_EVAL_LOCAL_ROOTS` is set independently of the bridge (`executor-base.ts:349-351`), so a kernel can have an artifacts root and no bridge. Before this patch, `read("artifact://N")` worked in that kernel; now it raises. The `read()` fallback in the prelude also calls the bridge, so it cannot recover. When no bridge is configured, the helper should go back to the local listing.
